chapters.title: An Example to All Believers
chapters.html:
1 Thessalonians 1

1Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace.

The Thessalonians' Faith

2We always thank God for all of you, remembering you in our prayers, constantly

3remembering before our God and Father your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.

4For we know, brothers loved by God, that He has chosen you,

5because our gospel came to you not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction, as you know what kind of men we proved to be among you for your sake.

6You became imitators of us and of the Lord, for you received the word in much trouble with the joy of the Holy Spirit,

7so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.

8For from you the word of the Lord has sounded out, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but your faith in God has gone out everywhere, so that we have no need to say anything.

9For they themselves report about us what kind of welcome we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,

10and to wait for His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead, Jesus, who rescues us from the wrath to come.

chapters.title: Paul's Work in Thessalonica
chapters.html:
1 Thessalonians 2

Like a Nurse, Like a Father

1For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.

2Though we had already suffered and been shamefully treated at Philippi, as you know, we had the courage in our God to tell you the gospel of God in a hard struggle.

3For our appeal does not come from error or impurity or deceit,

4but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not to please men, but to please God, who tests our hearts.

5For we never came with words of flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed, God is witness,

6nor did we seek glory from men, whether from you or from others,

7though we could have made demands as apostles of Christ. But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her own children.

8So, longing for you, we were glad to share with you not only the gospel of God but our own lives, because you had become dear to us.

9For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil: working night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.

10You are witnesses, and God also, how holy and righteous and blameless we were toward you believers,

11just as you know how, like a father with his own children, we treated each one of you,

12urging you and encouraging you and charging you to walk in a way worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.

Received as the Word of God

13For this reason we also thank God constantly, that when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but as what it truly is, the word of God, which is at work in you believers.

14For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Christ Jesus that are in Judea. You suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews,

15who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out. They displease God and oppose all men,

16hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so as always to fill up the measure of their sins. But wrath has come upon them at last.

Longing to See Them

17But since we were torn away from you, brothers, for a short time, in person not in heart, we were all the more eager, with great desire, to see you face to face,

18because we wanted to come to you, I, Paul, again and again, but Satan hindered us.

19For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at His coming? Is it not you?

20For you are our glory and joy.

Notes

  • vv14–15 "from the Jews, who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets" — hypo tōn Ioudaiōn. The sentence sets two persecutions side by side: the Thessalonians suffered from your own countrymen, as the churches in Judea did from the people of Judea. Ioudaioi is both Jews and Judeans. Paul, a Jew himself (Philippians 3:5), speaks of those who drove the gospel out, as Jesus said, Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets (Matthew 23:37).

chapters.title: Timothy's Good News
chapters.html:
1 Thessalonians 3

1So when we could bear it no longer, we thought it best to be left behind at Athens alone,

2and we sent Timothy, our brother and God's fellow worker in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and to encourage you in your faith,

3so that no one would be shaken by these troubles. For you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.

4For when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we were going to suffer trouble, just as it has happened, as you know.

5For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, for fear that the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.

Timothy's Report

6But now Timothy has come to us from you and has brought us the good news of your faith and love, and that you always remember us kindly and long to see us, as we long to see you.

7So, brothers, in all our distress and trouble we have been comforted about you through your faith.

8For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.

9For what thanks can we give to God for you, for all the joy we feel because of you before our God,

10as we pray night and day most earnestly to see you face to face and to supply what is lacking in your faith?

11Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you,

12and may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love for one another and for all, as we do for you,

13so that He may strengthen your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints.

chapters.title: The Coming of the Lord
chapters.html:
1 Thessalonians 4

A Life Pleasing to God

1Finally, then, brothers, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus that, as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, as you are doing, you do so more and more.

2For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.

3For this is the will of God, your holiness: that you keep away from sexual immorality,

4that each one of you know how to gain his own vessel in holiness and honor,

5not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God;

6that no one go too far and wrong his brother in this matter, because the Lord is the avenger in all these things, as we told you before and solemnly warned you.

7For God has not called us to impurity but in holiness.

8So whoever rejects this rejects not man but God, who gives His Holy Spirit to you.

9Now about love of the brothers, you have no need for anyone to write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another,

10and indeed you do it to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to do so more and more,

11and to make it your ambition to live quietly, to mind your own affairs, and to work with your hands, as we instructed you,

12so that you may walk properly before outsiders and be dependent on no one.

Those Who Have Fallen Asleep

13We do not want you to be uninformed, brothers, about those who are falling asleep, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.

14For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.

15For this we tell you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will not go before those who have fallen asleep.

16For the Lord Himself will come down from heaven with a cry of command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first.

17Then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will always be with the Lord.

18So comfort one another with these words.

Notes

  • v4 "gain his own vessel" — to heautou skeuos ktasthai. Skeuos, vessel, jar, is the body in we have this treasure in clay pots (2 Corinthians 4:7), and a wife in the wife as the weaker vessel (1 Peter 3:7); ktaomai is to acquire, and also to keep, to master. So the verse can mean learn to control your own body or take a wife of your own, in holiness and not in lust. Vessel keeps both.

  • v17 "caught up… to meet the Lord in the air" — eis apantēsin, the word for going out to meet someone on the road and coming back with him: the brothers… came as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet us (Acts 28:15, eis apantēsin). Those who are caught up go out to meet the Lord as He comes. Caught up is harpazō, the verb of Paul caught up to the third heaven (2 Corinthians 12:2).

chapters.title: Children of the Day
chapters.html:
1 Thessalonians 5

The Day of the Lord

1Now about the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you,

2for you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.

3While people are saying, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction will come on them, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.

4But you, brothers, are not in darkness, for that day to overtake you like a thief.

5For you are all sons of light and sons of the day. We are not of the night or of darkness.

6So then let us not sleep, as others do, but let us stay awake and be sober.

7For those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, are drunk at night.

8But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.

9For God has not appointed us for wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,

10who died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.

11So comfort one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.

Final Instructions

12We ask you, brothers, to respect those who labor among you and lead you in the Lord and warn you,

13and to hold them in the highest regard in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.

14We urge you, brothers: warn the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with everyone.

15See that no one repays evil for evil, but always seek what is good for one another and for everyone.

16Rejoice always,

17pray without ceasing,

18give thanks in everything; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

19Do not quench the Spirit;

20do not despise prophecies,

21but test everything; hold fast to what is good;

22keep away from every form of evil.

23May the God of peace Himself make you holy through and through, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

24He who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.

25Brothers, pray for us.

26Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.

27I charge you by the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.

28The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

Notes

  • v8 "the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation" — the armor the LORD puts on in Isaiah, righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of deliverance on His head (Isaiah 59:17), perikephalaian sōtēriou in the Greek. Paul gives it here to the believers, made of faith, love and hope, the three of 1:3.
